Perfume rating 3.69 out of 5 with 6,731 votes

Bitter Peach by Tom Ford is a Oriental Vanilla fragrance for women and men. Bitter Peach was launched in 2020. Top notes are Peach, Blood Orange, Cardamom and Heliotrope; middle notes are Rum, Cognac, Davana and Jasmine; base notes are Vanilla, Indonesian Patchouli Leaf, Tonka Bean, Sandalwood, Benzoin, Cashmeran, Styrax, Labdanum and Vetiver.

Tom Ford Bitter Peach is a part of the collection Private Blend, officially released in early October 2020.

Pêche de Vigne is mixed with Sicilian bloodd orange, davana oil with infused rum and cognac, Indonesian patchouli, sandalwood, labdanum and vanilla. The composition is described as sweet and sensual, but also rich and characterful, with pronounced woody and resinous undertones.

Tom Ford Bitter Peach is available as a 50, 100 and 250 ml Eau de Parfum.

luvoxlixir 09/16/25 23:58

So I revisited Bitter Peach, and oh is this a most re-orchestrated, redemptive review. With less suspicion and more skin, I found the whole thing to click into focus. It was less like the concoction of candied cough syrup I got last occasion, and more like an umbrous bruised peach radiating scarlet from its pit. Velvet flesh, tannic pit, a rind-level bitterness that keeps the sweetness from ever slumping. This scent is even... fuzzy.

Technically the peach is a sleight of hand folded into woody ionones: a synthetically sun-warmed, slightly shadowed fruit. If you're looking for photorealistic, safe to say this is not your best bet. The boozy halo however is gorgeous: I can see rum, cognac, slivovitz, inflections stitched together with balsams. Gives it almost a silk-lined swagger, really. There is definitely that smoky twang from davana too—almost reminds me of a herbal grapefruit tonic, actually—and a clever patchouli fraction, cocoa-dusty and dry. The sweet pith curve v. the bitter and lacquered edge. Ahh. There's that vibe of an amber lamp lighting up, while vanilla plays accompanist, maybe just one too close to turning the liqueur glow syrupy.

The balance is precarious. Spices brushed onto cashmere, labdanum incense brushing up on skin. Everything gives Bitter Peach a slouchy yet architectural build. One thing I definitely noticed: the cold keeps composition taut, the bitter line keeps the lactones honest. It's less pharmacy to my first experience, the sweetness now arriving in pulses then receding before fatigue. It’s still big (don't doubt, projecting in ellipses. One spray is plenty; two is a proclamation. Maybe it's not heat-proof, too charismatic for small talk, but it more than devotes to the sensuous, the luxurious, the slightly dangerous. A lot hypnotic: a slow fade of peel and warm woods, the fruit dimming to golden-hour memory while the bitter thread keeps glowing. Yes, absolutely.

thenakedchicken 09/09/25 00:41

Prominently powdery opening that reveals an almost astringent underripe fruit. The mid- and base notes modulate the sharpness of the citrus to effervescence.
The white florals may read feminine to some wearers, but I believe these notes are styled to unisex by the peach, citrus, and the dry, resinous base.
It's a clean, warm, and tactile scent that wouldn't be out of place if you're sat under a big, fluffy throw rug, three drinks deep watching Jamie Fraser stoke the fire.
Projection is about 4 or 5 feet, sillage is noticeable but not pushy. Longevity is the low end of good (6-8 hours).

I bought 100ml of this secondhand online for an extreme bargain, and after seeing the repeated comments concerning how overpriced bitter peach is - even among Tom Ford's already overpriced catalogue - I hoped I could offer perhaps a more even-handed review given that I only forked up 100$ CAD for the bottle.
Bitter Peach is fun. More specifically, it's the fun of a woman in her early thirties with more money than she knows what to do with. Immediately upon spraying, the smell is infectiously sweet, but not saccharine. I'm reminded of a cocktail which costs the same as a full meal and is served with a layer of foam on the top and a peach-skin garnish. It doesn't smell like a real peach in my opinion, but rather parts of a peach, or someone's very clever imagining of a peach. As the night went on, it developed into something warmer, spicier, and more masculine. Although I should mention, it remains a decidedly feminine fragrance. It's as if the big-shot businessman this disgustingly rich woman is hanging around with that day is rubbing his cologne and cigar smoke / rum smell off on her. There's something there I can't place, but I found myself smelling my wrist again and again, trying to figure it out - smiling every time.
Sure, there are perfumes which offer a more complex experience for the appalling price tag. Sure, there are perfumes which are more mature, more self-serious, etcetera. But, maybe I want to smell like someone who books a one-way ticket to Portofino on a whim and wears gold bracelets which cost the same as a down payment on a house, someone with a sweet infectious laugh and a love of fresh fruit.

TheDogfatherHTX 01/14/25 19:23

We're continuing our Tom Ford expedition today with Bitter Peach; that bright orange private blend bottle that sticks out like a neon sign in the line-up. I remember trying this one at Sephora and thinking it was okay, but nothing special. I mean it smelled like peaches, straight up. Not necessarily something I'd want to smell like during the course of the day, but I can appreciate what it does. I'm hoping that a full wearing will awaken something in the fragrance that makes it special. Let's get into it;

Scent:
The opening is sweet, fruity, and citrusy. The primary notes I get are peach, blood orange, vanilla, and rum. The strongest of the notes are the peach and vanilla. True to its name, the peach takes center stage in the opening with a sweet, fruity note very reminiscent of biting into a fresh peach. The vanilla then comes in behind for an extra dose of creamy sweetness. This is followed by the blood orange and rum. The blood orange is a distinct orange note nuanced by extra sweetness. Lastly, the rum is just the tiniest bit noticeable behind the other notes as a sweet and slightly boozy note in the background. The dry down is fruity, sweet, and woody. The primary notes I get are peach, vanilla, sandalwood, and cognac. The strongest of the notes are still the peach and vanilla. Both notes carry the same accords from the opening, with the primary difference being that the peach has taken a step back to let the vanilla lead the way. This is followed by the sandalwood and cognac. The sandalwood imparts a gentle and creamy woodiness to the dry down that compliments the vanilla. Lastly, the cognac brings a subtle booziness to background, similar to the rum in the opening but much sweeter and darker.

Performance:
Initial projection is average at about 3 feet. Sillage is below average with a modest scent trail. After a few hours the projection had died down to about arms length and the scent trail was still there, but only barely. The fragrance became a skin scent shortly after that.

When to wear:
Bitter Peach is a fragrance that is best suited for daytime wear, but can be worn for virtually any season. The peach note makes it great for warmer weather, while the vanilla works well for cooler weather. This is more of a casual wearing fragrance, not something I would pick for anything formal or for office wear.

Blind buy:
If the thought of smelling like peaches and cream appeals to you, this is a safe blind buy. Just keep in mind that you'll need to spray heavy and re-apply every few hours.

Final verdict:
So Bitter Peach was a pretty big letdown, as I imagined it might be. The scent profile is good, albeit way too feminine for me. Peaches and vanilla is great, but not something most men will want to smell like. But again, just like with the Tobacco Oud I reviewed yesterday, the performance was dismal. Even worse than Tobacco Oud, honestly. Even from the first spray the projection and sillage were modest at best, and the fragrance was all but gone within a few hours. Versatility is above average, which is nice. Pretty much any time outside of formal this will feel appropriate. Mass appeal is there too, almost everyone will think this DNA smells good. But really when it comes down to it, the amount you'll have to overspray to get even decent performance from this will have you running through the bottle quick. And with a price of over $400 for only 50mls, this is a huge money drain. If you like this DNA just grab one of the clones; Bitter Peach ain't worth the money.

Scent: 7/10
Longevity: 5/10
Sillage: 5/10

JoyDivision 10/31/24 15:13

Tom Ford’s Bitter Peach opens with a burst of luscious, ripe peach—both juicy and slightly dry, giving off an alluring, boozy edge that feels decadent and rich. This initial splash is tinged with the warmth of brandy, as though the fruit were soaked in a heady cocktail, evoking both sweetness and a faint hint of bitterness.

As it settles, Bitter Peach reveals layers of sweetness that are far from cloying, thanks to laudanum and styrax, which bring a resinous, smoky depth. Benzoin adds a touch of soft warmth, wrapping around the peachy notes like a rich, balsamic hug. The vanilla and tonka bean then emerge, blending with the fruity heart to create an intoxicating creaminess that balances the dry opening with velvety, gourmand richness. The result is a complex, seductive fragrance that dances between sweetness, spice, and a bittersweet edge—bold, opulent, and undeniably unforgettable.

evavidal62 06/22/24 19:17

This is a beautiful fragrance. I received a complimentary spray sample in a vial with my purchase of Jasmine Rouge at the Macy's on Herald Square in New York City. This is a spring and summer scent. Starts off fruity with a distinct peach note. It's a deep juicy peach. The aromatic green notes come rather quickly. Smells like green leaves, very herbal, with davana, vetiver and very strong patchouli. Ultimately, it's mainly and mostly peach and patchouli. Peachouli ...!!! If you like both those notes and can handle them, this wears quite well. It reminds me of a grove of peach trees beneath the warm sunshine. It is also coming through as a kind of still painting like those Dutch masters - Vermeer, Rembrandt, etc, with a simple depiction of a fruit bowl or a peach sliced open. It is bitter because of the green accords but the pairing of sweet peach and the patchouli give it a graphic photorealistic effect. The dry down notes are harder to pick out but I can detect the rum and cognac in small doses, some of the vanilla and some of the wood and benzoin. The hodgepodge of these notes give it that bitter (but not terribly bitter) effect. Aromatic is another word to describe this aroma. I would call this unisex and feminine at the same time. An occasion to wear it would be going to the museum (again I feel it is like a painting come to life) to a park, to a public garden, to a nature hike, a national forest. It is not tropical, but it is outdoorsy and meant to be worn outdoors in spring or summer. Quite nice. I was very enchanted with it and will buy a full bottle. I much prefer peach to vanilla. This peach has a lot of character and lots going on to make it a special peach centered perfume.

the real magic of this is when that patchouli mellows out and the scent becomes a cognac/rum type of peach. it definitely gives me a surprisingly sweet peach Hennessy type of vibe. i can see how it’s a more grown-up type of fruity scent without smelling like a grandparent. if you’re like me who was expecting a bright peach type of scent, this isn’t it but it is a nice scent nonetheless. definitely warms up/sweetens better on your skin. i made the mistake of spraying it on my clothes and it took hours for the cardamom and patchouli notes to mellow out.

Most Popular Positive Reviews

los benjos 08/10/21 22:17

A brief bit of background before we get into the scent. In Prague with my wife, we dip into a perfumery as she wants to check out something. I’m used to this being a relatively long process so gravitate over to the TF counter. The wife just bought a Killian bamboo (very nice) and I’m looking at the private blends. Just for fun, I pick up the bitter peach (it’s a hot day) expecting it to be very feminine and not for me. To start with I’m going to offer this advice. There’s a lot of noise about this fragrance, so you need to put all that to the side and just try it on your skin.

First spritz: a really intense hit of bitter peach and orange. Very nice on a warm summer evening. Fun. And I liked it a lot. But having made quick decisions before and regretted as things dry down (and given the price point), I let my wife smell it (she really liked it on me) and we went to have a drink and a walk.

This is where things got interesting. I sniffed my arm intermittently. And I liked it even more. After a good 2 hours my wife is noticing during aperitif that I’m sniffing and smiling. A lot.

The dry down on this is what makes it. You are left with that peachiness but it develops into a woody, faintly floral and slightly amber skin scent. It’s morning here and I just smelled my arm again. It’s still there, faint but really, genuinely very, very good.

To me this is perfectly unisex, and I would argue that the Drydown makes it lean more masculine.

And it’s fun. It’s really fun. It makes me smile. And it’s been a long time since I smelled my arm and smiled repeatedly.

Is it worth the price point. As I said to my wife: “That b@stard Ford has done it again”, he makes perfumes that I consistently reach for, that challenge and make me smile, and that I really enjoy smelling on me. They happen to be expensive. Which is clearly a pisser.

I don’t know what made me reach for the bitter peach, maybe just a whim, the colour, the heat, the fact that I’m quite partial to a peach ice-tea, but I’m very glad I did.

I went back and bought a bottle, luckily my wife had a discount of 15% which helped a bit.

I’ll leave it here: try it, all of our skin chemistries are different, and some of love smells and tastes that others don’t, are indifferent about or find repulsive.

I find value judgements about the TF brand largely irrelevant to the conversation, was it better before, has it sold out? Honestly my dear fragrance lovers, who cares?

What I care about is smelling nice and fragrances that lift, make me happy and that I enjoy wearing. Bitter peach is now part of that roster.

ginandrice 10/19/20 23:50

If this were a quarter of the price, I would be into it. It’s the olfactory equivalent of eating a peach-flavored Jelly Belly. It’s peach, through and through; distilled, sugary, and with a peach-fuzz vibe that’s most likely conveyed by the sandalwood and cashmeran.

The trouble, for me, is that no matter how many notes are in this, all I really get is PEACH. It smells youthful, juicy, sweet, and sort of playful. Which would be fine, if this were a $90 fragrance, but for Tom Ford prices, I want complexity and depth, not a one-note bit of fun.

I will say, I love Angel, and this smells almost nothing like Angel to me. At leas not the EDP. It may have just a little resemblance to the Angel EDT. The peach here is juicy&sweet&tangy in a way that is broadly similar to the juicy&sweet&tangy of red berries, praline, and vanilla in Angel EDT's opening. But Angel EDT is much funkier and more gourmandish than BP’s overwhelming juicy peach note.

Deutsch100 10/09/20 16:48

My Bitter Peach arrived from Nordstrom New York City, and I am in LOVE!! I have 8-9 Tom Ford scents (my favs are Tobacco Vanille, Lost Cherry and Noir de Noir) and I am quite sure Bitter Peach will be in my top 3-4 fav scents.

Initial spray is strong and V E R Y peachy, almost peach rings candy peachy (good thing I happen to absolutely love peach rings ;) ) While the peach scent is very strong and almost realistic and very sweet, it is not a juvenile sweet.

Within 10-15 mins, the very strong and sweet peach candy note softens, and like magic...Bitter Peach warms up, softens and woody and balsamic notes take the wheel.

I was so nervous after that Fragrantica writer bashed Bitter Peach, and maybe it was done because of the stupid high price (yes, it is overpriced), but Bitter Peach is magical. I cannot stop smelling my arm. 1-2 sprays on my arm, and 4 hours later...it has softened but is still very there and smells even better.

Nraveles 09/14/20 19:35

So I just got a bottle today and sprayed it on a small spot on my arm. The first initial spray was decently harsh, could throw some people off. It lives up to the “bitter” in the name, but definitely isn’t horrendous, I actually enjoyed it. The main thing you smell is definitely peach, obviously. It’s very very realistic which is kinda crazy? It isn’t your typical syrupy or overly sweet peach, it’s like a peach you just picked, juicy, fragrant, and just perfectly ripe. I literally just smell a very juicy peach in this, and I’m not the biggest peach fan with fragrances.

As it dries down, you get a bit of extra freshness which is really nice. The sandalwood comes in for a good creamy bit of richness to it. I still think the craziest thing is how the peach actually stays the entire time. Usually a peach note would just kinda fly away after the first 15-20 minutes at most but it’s there the entire time.

I can say I thoroughly enjoy this. Performance is way better than Lost Cherry, and isn’t as thick or syrupy. It’s a lot more fresh and bright. This is a perfect summer or early fall fragrance. The only thing that keeps me from fully recommending is the price, but if you can get your hands on it, you won’t be disappointed. I absolutely love it.

It was just 1 spritz and I could smell it all day around me Even tho i wasnt smelling my wrist, so longevity and sillage is pretty good. Leans more feminine in my opinion. Overall it is a good fragrance and in my opinion a good adition to the line because its completely different than the other private blends.

Jay67 10/02/20 00:27

Tested this yesterday in Selfridges and to be perfectly honest, it confused the hell out of me. I’m kind of not surprised at TF/Lauder releasing another of these “fruit”/sweet frags; it seems to be the way they are going now but for me personally, with 8 or so Private Blends in my collection, I can’t see me buying many more if they carry on down this road.

One big piece of advice I would have when you try this; make sure you test on skin AND paper because they truly are two completely different experiences! On paper, you get an very sweet peach, almost like a confectioners peach to the nose or a cocktail peach purée but on skin, the name, Bitter Peach, truly does apply: polar opposites! I honestly wasn’t keen on the heliotrope - orange combo in the opening and was scratching my head over the cashmeran in the base..... just couldn’t work out why you would?! Also for me, the Davana in the mid is far too screechy & the boozy notes don’t seem to offer up much to temper that; I barely knew they were there at all.

So, it’s a mild dislike from me I’m afraid. Estée Lauder seem to be buying up a lot of niche/private line frags that once held a vaunted place in the community and reformulating the hell out of them or putting out such mediocre releases that I really do question where they’re going with it and at the same time, discontinuing loved and respected ones. I just don’t get it I’m afraid!

tandem_4x4 11/11/20 20:54

It arrived to Australian David Jones today. I did not expect anything groundbreaking after Rose Prick, which I find rather ordinary rose perfume.

Bitter Peach is not ordinary, for sure. However it performs very strange:
- First 30 seconds is it like Yvresse by YSL - brewed peach.
- Then it turns to something extremely bitter, which no peach at all - lets call it "bitter almond". The "bitter almond" stays for about 5 minute.
- After that it becomes bottom notes of vintage Angel - patchouli with no sweetness but with what we call "chocolate" in perfumery. And again: with no traces of peach or bitterness. This stays for another 5 minutes.
- And following it the smell turns to the Angel base with cat pee on top. It is for 10 minutes.
- Finally all this cacophony becomes a very quiet generic perfume, sitting so close to the skin that no-one can feel it at all.

I generally like almost all perfumes, and even appreciate those I hate. But I really can not appreciate perfumes without DNAs. This one fall apart to at least 5 different scents and does it pretty quickly. Also longevity and projection are very poor. Not sure if I am ready to pay AU$480 for something like this. Preempting some thoughts: I can afford it and have ~500 bottles of perfumes, including most of Tom Ford. This one does not appeal to me.

What I really appreciate - the idea. If this fragrance was blended well, it would be to die for. And no ambroxan - these days it deserves the special prize. Probably (read) TF (think) Estee Lauder can properly blend it. Then I will be running to the David Jones to grab it and wear it. Although, who cares, TF sells like hotdogs whatever you put in the bottle.

PS: Also seems some reviews below are from people who were not wearing the fragrance and likely only tried it on the blotter or from the bottle. I would summarize reviews below:
- those who like it and say "peach" likely did not see the development of the fragrance while wearing.
- those who said "Angel" were actually wearing the fragrance and understand the whole performance.
Therefore, those who read it - do not blind buy: test it first and test it properly on the skin. Make your judgement after 1 hour of wearing.

EDIT: i tried it today when weather is getting colder in Australia. The good news: composition does not fall apart anymore. The bad news: it is a bitter cat pee now. Shall I call it "Bitter Pee"? I will try it again in about 3 months. Still trying to find the beauty in this fragrance.
